The New Adam & the New Eve

how the first man and woman, the throne of David, and the Ark of the Covenant foreshadow Christ and his Mother

“The New Testament lies hidden in the Old, and the Old is unveiled in the New.”

— St. Augustine (CCC 129)
I

In the Beginning

the first man and woman · 4 parallels
The New Adam Adam → Jesus Christ

Old Covenant · the type

Adam

the first man, formed from the dust of the ground

“by one man's disobedience many were made sinners”

Gen 2:7 · Rom 5:12, 19

The Parallel · what links them

The New Adam

Adam “was a type of the one who was to come”

“The first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.”

Rom 5:14 · 1 Cor 15:22, 45 · CCC 411, 504

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Jesus Christ

the last Adam, the man from heaven, who begins the new creation

“by one man's obedience many will be made righteous”

Rom 5:19 · 1 Cor 15:47

The New Eve Eve → Mary

Old Covenant · the type

Eve

the first woman, formed from Adam's side

a virgin, she listened to the serpent and disobeyed

Gen 2:21–22; 3:1–6

The Parallel · what links them

The New Eve

“the knot of Eve's disobedience was loosed by the obedience of Mary”

— St. Irenaeus, c. 180

“Death through Eve, life through Mary.”

— the Fathers

St. Justin, Dialogue 100 · CCC 411, 494, 726

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Mary

a virgin, she listened to the angel and obeyed

“let it be to me according to your word”

Lk 1:26–38

At Her Urging The First Sin → The First Sign

Old Covenant · the type

The First Sin

in the garden of Eden

Eve takes the fruit and eats; “she also gave some to her husband … and he ate”

their eyes are opened: shame, exile from the garden, death

Gen 3:6–7, 19, 23

The Parallel · what links them

At Her Urging

In Eden, at Eve's urging, Adam commits the first sin.

At Cana, at Mary's urging, Jesus performs his first sign.

Eve led her husband away from God's word; Mary points to it: “Do whatever he tells you.”

Gen 3:6 · Jn 2:3–5, 11 · CCC 1613, 2618

New Covenant · the fulfillment

The First Sign

the wedding at Cana

at the wedding feast Mary tells him, “They have no wine,” and tells the servants, “Do whatever he tells you”

water becomes wine, “the first of his signs”: he “manifested his glory; and his disciples believed in him”

Jn 2:1–11

Woman “Woman” → “Woman”

Old Covenant · the type

“Woman”

אִשָּׁה ’ishshah

“she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man”

through the whole story of the Fall she is simply “the woman” — only afterward is she named Eve

“I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed”

Gen 2:23; 3:1–16, 20

The Parallel · what links them

Woman

Jesus calls his mother not “Mother” but “Woman” — the name of Eve before the Fall

Mary is the Woman of the first Gospel, at enmity with the serpent (Gen 3:15)

CCC 410–411, 726

New Covenant · the fulfillment

“Woman”

γύναι gynai

at Cana: “Woman, … my hour has not yet come”

at the Cross, when the hour has come: “Woman, behold, your son!”

Jn 2:4; 19:26

II

The Throne of David

the king and the queen mother · 2 parallels
The King Solomon → Christ the King

Old Covenant · the type

Solomon

son of David, king of Israel

seated on the throne of David

God's promise to David's son: “I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever”

2 Sam 7:12–16 · 1 Kgs 2:12

The Parallel · what links them

The King

the promise to David's son is fulfilled in the everlasting reign of Christ

Mt 1:1 · Lk 1:32–33 · CCC 439

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Christ the King

Jesus, Son of David

“the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David … and of his kingdom there will be no end”

Lk 1:32–33

The Queen Mother Bathsheba → Queen of Heaven

Old Covenant · the type

Bathsheba

mother of King Solomon

גְּבִירָה gebirah, “great lady”

in the house of David the queen was the king's mother, not his wife: Solomon had 700 wives, but one mother

the king rises to meet her, bows, and sets a throne for her at his right hand; she brings petitions to the king

1 Kgs 2:19–20; 11:3; 15:13 · Jer 13:18

The Parallel · what links them

The Queen Mother

the Son of David reigns for ever, and the queen of his kingdom is his mother

as Bathsheba brought petitions to Solomon, Mary brings our needs to her Son

Jn 2:3 · CCC 966, 969 · Ad Caeli Reginam

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Queen of Heaven

Mary, mother of the King

Elizabeth greets her as “the mother of my Lord”

“a woman clothed with the sun … on her head a crown of twelve stars”

assumed into heaven and “exalted by the Lord as Queen over all things”

Lk 1:43 · Rev 12:1 · CCC 966

III

The Ark of the Covenant

God's dwelling among his people · 5 parallels
The New Ark The Ark → Mary

Old Covenant · the type

The Ark

of the covenant, in the Holy of Holies

a chest overlaid with gold; above it, between the cherubim, God met with his people

“There I will meet with you”

Ex 25:10–22 · 1 Kgs 8:6–11

The Parallel · what links them

The New Ark

the ark held God's presence among his people; for nine months God himself dwelt within Mary

Mary is “the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells”

CCC 2676 · Litany of Loreto: “Ark of the Covenant”

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Mary

the living ark

God makes his dwelling not in a chest of wood and gold, but in her womb

“the Word became flesh and dwelt among us”

ἐσκήνωσεν eskēnōsen, “pitched his tent”

Jn 1:14 · Lk 1:31

What She Carried What the Ark Held → What Mary Carried

Old Covenant · the type

What the Ark Held

the tablets of the Law
the word of God, written in stone

a golden jar of manna
bread from heaven in the wilderness

Aaron's rod that budded
sign of the true priesthood

Heb 9:4 · Deut 10:5 · Ex 16:33–34 · Num 17:8–10

The Parallel · what links them

What She Carried

the ark carried signs; Mary carried the One they signified

the Law → the Word
the manna → the Bread of Life
the priestly rod → the High Priest

Heb 9:4

New Covenant · the fulfillment

What Mary Carried

the Word of God
made flesh

the living bread
come down from heaven

the eternal high priest
who holds his priesthood for ever

Jn 1:14 · Jn 6:51 · Heb 4:14; 7:24

Overshadowed The Glory Cloud → The Annunciation

Old Covenant · the type

The Glory Cloud

over the tabernacle

“the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle”

ἐπεσκίαζεν epeskiazen, “overshadowed”

Ex 40:34–35 (LXX)

The Parallel · what links them

Overshadowed

the same Greek verb describes the glory cloud over the tabernacle and the Spirit over Mary

where God's glory rests, there God dwells

Ex 40:35 (LXX) · Lk 1:35 · CCC 697

New Covenant · the fulfillment

The Annunciation

over the Virgin

“The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you”

ἐπισκιάσει episkiasei, “will overshadow”

Lk 1:35

Incorruptible A Holy Vessel → Full of Grace

Old Covenant · the type

A Holy Vessel

made of acacia, “wood that does not decay” in the Greek, overlaid with pure gold within and without

so holy that Uzzah, touching it, was struck dead

“Arise, O LORD, and go to thy resting place, thou and the ark of thy might”

Ex 25:10–11 (LXX) · 2 Sam 6:6–7 · Ps 132:8

The Parallel · what links them

Incorruptible

Pius XII: the ark of incorruptible wood is “a type of the most pure body of the Virgin Mary,” preserved from the corruption of the tomb

Munificentissimus Deus 26 · Ps 132:8

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Full of Grace

immaculate, and assumed into heaven

preserved from every stain of sin from her conception

at the end of her earthly life, taken body and soul into heavenly glory

Lk 1:28 · CCC 491–492, 966

The Ark Revealed The Lost Ark → The Ark in Heaven

Old Covenant · the type

The Lost Ark

before the Babylonian exile, Jeremiah hid the ark in a cave

“The place shall be unknown until God gathers his people together again”

2 Macc 2:4–8

The Parallel · what links them

The Ark Revealed

John sees the lost ark in heaven, and the very next thing he sees is the Woman

the chapter break between them was added only in the 13th century

Rev 11:19 – 12:1

New Covenant · the fulfillment

The Ark in Heaven

“God's temple in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant was seen within his temple …”

“And a great portent appeared in heaven, a woman clothed with the sun”

Rev 11:19 – 12:1

IV

The Ark Goes Up to Judah

2 Samuel 6 and the Visitation, Luke 1:39–56 · 4 parallels
Arose and Went David Sets Out → Mary Sets Out

Old Covenant · the type

David Sets Out

“David arose and went … to bring up from there the ark of God”

from Baale-judah, in Judah

2 Sam 6:2 · 1 Chr 13:6

The Parallel · what links them

Arose and Went

the same words open both journeys, and both go into Judah

2 Sam 6:2 · Lk 1:39

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Mary Sets Out

“Mary arose and went with haste into the hill country, to a city of Judah”

Lk 1:39

“Come to Me?” David Asks → Elizabeth Asks

Old Covenant · the type

David Asks

afraid of the LORD after Uzzah's death

“How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”

2 Sam 6:9

The Parallel · what links them

“Come to Me?”

David asks how the ark could come to him; Elizabeth asks the same of Mary

“Mary's visitation to Elizabeth thus became a visit from God to his people”

2 Sam 6:9 · Lk 1:43 · CCC 717

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Elizabeth Asks

“why is this granted me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?”

Lk 1:43

Leaping for Joy David Dances → John Leaps

Old Covenant · the type

David Dances

“David danced before the LORD with all his might”

“leaping and dancing before the LORD,” while the Levites raise their voices with music before the ark

2 Sam 6:14–16 · 1 Chr 15:28; 16:4–5

The Parallel · what links them

Leaping for Joy

David leaps before the ark; John leaps before the One whom Mary carries

2 Sam 6:16 · Lk 1:41, 44

New Covenant · the fulfillment

John Leaps

“the babe in my womb leaped for joy”

Elizabeth “exclaimed with a loud cry”: a rare Greek verb that the LXX uses for the Levites' music before the ark

ἀνεφώνησεν anephōnēsen

Lk 1:41–44 · cf. 1 Chr 15:28 (LXX)

A House Blessed Three Months → Three Months

Old Covenant · the type

Three Months

in the house of Obed-edom

“the ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom … three months; and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household”

2 Sam 6:10–12

The Parallel · what links them

A House Blessed

the ark stays three months and blesses the house that receives it; so does Mary

2 Sam 6:11 · Lk 1:41–42, 56

New Covenant · the fulfillment

Three Months

in the house of Zechariah

“Mary remained with her about three months”

Elizabeth is “filled with the Holy Spirit”: “Blessed are you among women”

Lk 1:40–42, 56

Scripture quotations follow the RSV. CCC = Catechism of the Catholic Church. LXX = Septuagint, the Greek Old Testament.
